Funding & Partnerships

Supported by agencies who care about California agriculture.

Our research is funded by USGS, USDA-linked commodity boards, the CSU system, and the U.S. Department of Energy. Total competitive funding as PI or Co-PI: approximately $208,000.

Current

Active Grants & Beamtime

California Institute of Water Resources (CIWR) / USGS

Testing Proximal Sensor Technology to Improve Irrigation Use Efficiency for Vegetable Production in the Salinas Valley

$49,999

2025–2027

Role: Principal Investigator

Field-based project integrating proximal sensing and irrigation management to improve water-use efficiency in coastal vegetable production.

California Leafy Greens Research Board

USDA Lettuce Breeding for Improved Disease Resistance

$91,405 total (multi-institution)

2025–2027

Role: Co-PI, Site PI at CSUMB

Multi-institution collaboration linking xylem anatomy and plant physiology to Fusarium wilt resistance in lettuce breeding lines.

CSU Agricultural Research Institute (ARI)

Monitoring Soil Health, Water Conservation, and Vegetable Productivity on Organic Cropland Amended with Eucalyptus Biochar

$61,000

2024–2026

Role: Co-Principal Investigator

Evaluates biochar impacts on soil health, water conservation, and productivity in certified organic vegetable systems.

Advanced Light Source, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (DOE)

Exploring the Role of Conduit Implosion in Plants' Response to Drought and Disease — ALS Beamline 8.3.2

6 beamline shifts (General User Proposal)

2025–2026

Role: Experiment Leader

High-resolution synchrotron microCT of xylem conduit collapse and hydraulic failure under drought and pathogen infection.

Advanced Light Source, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (DOE)

Investigating Plant Traits Associated with Disease Resistance in Lettuce — ALS Beamline 8.3.2

9 beamline shifts (RAPIDD Allocation)

2025–2026

Role: Principal Investigator and Experiment Leader

Uses synchrotron microCT to link 3D xylem and tissue traits to Fusarium wilt resistance in lettuce lines.

Advanced Light Source · Lawrence Berkeley National Lab

Synchrotron beamtime is competitive. We have it.

Access to beamline 8.3.2 at the ALS requires a highly competitive proposal process. We currently hold 15 shifts across two active allocations — both led by our lab — giving us access to the world-class X-ray microCT infrastructure needed to image xylem anatomy and collapse at resolutions impossible with conventional microscopy.
